edges.effect_quant: Timing and baseline sleep disorder status strongly influence the size of the effect.
edges.mechanism: Short sleep duration (<6h) likely affects All-cause mortality through circadian timing, arousal signaling, upper-airway physiology, thermoregulation, or melatonin dynamics. Because sleep responses vary substantially across individuals, the same exposure can look mild in one group and much more disruptive in another.
edges.summary: Short sleep duration (<6h) is generally harmful for All-cause mortality in general adult, with the strongest signal around timing and individual sensitivity rather than a huge universal effect. Randomized sleep-lab work often supports the basic direction, while longer-term consequences mostly rely on cohort evidence. The practical message is usually about nudging sleep architecture or circadian alignment, not transforming sleep overnight.
edges.caveats: Timing, chronotype, dose, and baseline sleep problems matter. Short laboratory studies can overestimate acute effects, whereas observational sleep data may be confounded by shift schedules, mental health, alcohol use, or chronic disease.
